title: Review
description: One contract review: its findings, or its progress toward them.

id.title: Id
id.description: Public identifier, `rev_` followed by 32 hex characters.

matterId.title: Matterid
matterId.description: `mat_` identifier of the matter this review belongs to.

status.description: Review status, using the same five public values as an operation. While `queued` or `running`, every findings list is empty and the scalar fields are absent. That is the truthful shape of a review that has not happened yet, not an error.

contractType.title: Contracttype
contractType.description: Contract type the review ran as, echoed from the request.

userSide.title: Userside
userSide.description: Which side the review argued for, echoed from the request.

playbookId.title: Playbookid
playbookId.description: The playbook the review actually ran against. Absent when it ran against the built-in defaults, so the two cases can be told apart after the fact.

round.title: Round
round.description: Negotiation round this review was run for.

summary.title: Summary
summary.description: Prose summary of the review's conclusions.

overallRisk.title: Overallrisk
overallRisk.description: Overall risk rating for the contract: `green`, `yellow` or `red`.

businessImpactSummary.title: Businessimpactsummary
businessImpactSummary.description: What the findings mean commercially, in plain language.

approvalGate.description: Whether a human should sign this off before it goes out. Reported, never enforced.

liabilityExposure.description: How much you are on the hook for: caps, carve-outs, indemnities and insurance.

counterpartyMatch.description: Set when a known counterparty paper was recognized, which means the findings include counterparty-specific redlines layered on the general analysis.

clauses.title: Clauses
clauses.description: Every clause analyzed, with its severity against the playbook position.

redlines.title: Redlines
redlines.description: Proposed edits, ready to send to counterparty counsel. Check each one's `grounding` before applying it automatically.

negotiationPriorities.title: Negotiationpriorities
negotiationPriorities.description: What to raise first and what to trade, in tiers.

missingClauses.title: Missingclauses
missingClauses.description: Standard clauses ABSENT from the contract. The one finding that cannot be expressed as a clause analysis, because there is no clause to analyze.

flags.title: Flags
flags.description: Things the reviewer noticed and deliberately did not redline: a wrong entity name, an odd schedule entry, a real ambiguity. Confirm these with a human before signing.

parseWarning.title: Parsewarning
parseWarning.description: Set when the model's output only partly parsed, which means the findings may be incomplete. Present is the difference between acting on the findings and asking a human first.

deep.description: What the deep verification pass did. Absent on a standard review, which is the signal that no verification ran rather than that it found nothing.

completedAt.title: Completedat
completedAt.description: When the review reached a terminal status (RFC 3339).

OperationStatus.title: OperationStatus
OperationStatus.description:
The public five. There is no sixth, and there are no synonyms.

Internal vocabularies spell terminal success `completed`, `ready`,
`extracted`, `succeeded` and `fresh`; terminal failure `failed` and `error`;
queued `pending`, `queued` and `draft`. All of that is collapsed here by
`app.workspace_api.adapters.status_map`, which refuses to guess.

required.title: Required
required.description: Whether a human should sign this off before it goes to the counterparty. REPORTED, never enforced: it does not block the review or the export. Implement the gate on your side using this field.

level.title: Level
level.description: The highest sign-off any gating clause needs: `manager`, `partner` or `gc`. Absent when `required` is false.

dealBreakerCount.title: Dealbreakercount
dealBreakerCount.description: How many clauses sit at or below the walk-away floor.

reasons.title: Reasons
reasons.description: Which clauses drive the gate, and why each one does.

summary.title: Summary
summary.description: One-line explanation of the gate, suitable to show a reviewer.

ReviewApprovalGate.title: ReviewApprovalGate
ReviewApprovalGate.description:
Whether a human has to sign this off before it goes to the counterparty.

**Reported, never enforced.** The gate is computed deterministically from the
playbook's own `approvalLevel` and `dealBreaker` on clauses that actually
deviated, and it is published as a fact about the result. It does not block
the review, it does not block the export, and the operation reaches a
terminal status either way.

That is the same decision the acting-user header already carries (docs 07.3):
we record what we know and build no enforcement machinery we cannot honour.
Enforcing would mean an approval workflow, an enrolled approver directory and
a state a review can sit in indefinitely, which is precisely the "do not let
it hang" failure the handoff for this track warned about. A caller that wants
a gate has everything it needs to implement one: `required` says whether,
`level` says who, and `reasons` says why.

clauseName.title: Clausename
clauseName.description: The clause driving this part of the gate.

isDealBreaker.title: Isdealbreaker
isDealBreaker.description: True when this clause is at or below the walk-away floor.

note.title: Note
note.description: Set when a conditional rule RAISED this clause's sign-off, for example 'Escalated to GC: deal value over $1M'. Absent when the level came straight from the playbook position.

ReviewApprovalReason.title: ReviewApprovalReason
ReviewApprovalReason.description: One clause driving the review-level sign-off gate.

clauseName.title: Clausename
clauseName.description: Human-readable name of the clause, for example 'Limitation of Liability'.

clauseType.title: Clausetype
clauseType.description: Clause-type slug the analysis matched, the same key a playbook's `positions` map uses.

sectionReference.title: Sectionreference
sectionReference.description: Where the clause sits in the contract, for example `8.2`.

currentLanguage.title: Currentlanguage
currentLanguage.description: The exact quote from the contract this analysis is about. Empty when the finding is that the clause is ABSENT, which is the one case with nothing to quote.

severity.title: Severity
severity.description: How far the clause deviates from the playbook position: `green`, `yellow` or `red`. Published as a plain string so a new level cannot break your client.

analysis.title: Analysis
analysis.description: What the reviewer concluded about this clause.

riskDescription.title: Riskdescription
riskDescription.description: What could go wrong if the clause stands as written.

playbookPosition.title: Playbookposition
playbookPosition.description: The playbook position this clause was measured against.

approvalLevel.title: Approvallevel
approvalLevel.description: Sign-off a deviation on this clause needs: `none`, `manager`, `partner` or `gc`. Computed server-side by matching the clause to its playbook position, never asserted by the model. Only meaningful when `severity` is not green.

isDealBreaker.title: Isdealbreaker
isDealBreaker.description: True when the clause is at or below the playbook's walk-away floor.

ReviewClause.title: ReviewClause
ReviewClause.description: One clause, as analyzed against the playbook position for its type.

name.title: Name
name.description: Name of the recognized counterparty paper.

vendor.title: Vendor
vendor.description: The vendor whose standard form this is.

flexibility.title: Flexibility
flexibility.description: How negotiable this paper is in practice: `rigid`, `limited` or `standard`.

negotiationStrategyNote.title: Negotiationstrategynote
negotiationStrategyNote.description: How to approach negotiating against this specific paper.

counterpartyRedlinesCount.title: Counterpartyredlinescount
counterpartyRedlinesCount.description: How many redlines the counterparty overlay contributed on top of the general analysis. A non-zero value means the findings are tuned to this specific paper.

ReviewCounterpartyMatch.title: ReviewCounterpartyMatch
ReviewCounterpartyMatch.description:
A known counterparty paper was recognised in the contract text.

Published so a caller knows the findings include counterparty-specific
redlines layered on top of the general analysis, which changes how the result
should be read. The catalogue slug and the phrases that matched are NOT
published: they are our detection internals, and neither is actionable.

clausesReviewed.title: Clausesreviewed
clausesReviewed.description: How many first-pass flagged clauses the deep pass verified.

redlinesKept.title: Redlineskept
redlinesKept.description: How many survived verification and are in `redlines`.

clearedAsCompliant.title: Clearedascompliant
clearedAsCompliant.description: How many first-pass flags the deep pass cleared as already compliant, and therefore dropped. Fewer false positives is the point of running deep.

clauseLimit.title: Clauselimit
clauseLimit.description: The ceiling on how many flagged clauses a deep review verifies, currently 40.

clausesTruncated.title: Clausestruncated
clausesTruncated.description: True when the deep pass hit its 40-clause ceiling, which means first-pass flags beyond it were NOT verified and are NOT in `redlines`. Treat the review as covering the first 40 findings only. A boolean rather than a count because the number dropped is not recorded anywhere upstream.

ReviewDeepMeta.title: ReviewDeepMeta
ReviewDeepMeta.description:
What the deep verification pass did, present only when one ran.

Absent on a standard review, which is the honest signal that no verification
happened rather than a zeroed object implying one found nothing.

`estimatedCostUsd` is dropped on the way through. It is our spend and our
model choice, and it is on the list of things a published DTO always drops.

clauseName.title: Clausename
clauseName.description: Which clause or part of the contract the observation is about.

sectionReference.title: Sectionreference
sectionReference.description: Where it sits in the contract.

observation.title: Observation
observation.description: What the reviewer noticed. These are things a human should confirm before signing, not edits, which makes them the most important field here for a caller automating the review away.

ReviewFlag.title: ReviewFlag
ReviewFlag.description:
Something the reviewer noticed and deliberately did NOT redline.

A wrong entity name, an odd schedule entry, a real ambiguity. These are not
edits; they are things a human should confirm before signing, which makes
them the most important thing on this surface for a caller that is otherwise
automating the review away.

exposureLevel.title: Exposurelevel
exposureLevel.description: Overall liability exposure from your side: `green`, `yellow` or `red`.

verdict.title: Verdict
verdict.description: Plain-language summary of the liability position.

capStatus.title: Capstatus
capStatus.description: Whether liability is capped: `capped`, `uncapped`, `partial` or `not_addressed`. Null when it could not be determined.

capAmount.title: Capamount
capAmount.description: The cap as written, as a string rather than a number since contracts express it in many forms (a figure, a multiple of fees, a formula).

capQuote.title: Capquote
capQuote.description: The verbatim contract sentence the cap claim is drawn from, so a headline number can be checked against the source rather than trusted.

grounding.title: Grounding
grounding.description: `verified` when `capQuote` is a literal span of the contract, `unverified` when it could not be found. Same meaning as on a redline.

capScope.title: Capscope
capScope.description: What the cap applies across: `per_claim`, `aggregate`, `both` or `unclear`.

capAdequate.title: Capadequate
capAdequate.description: Whether the cap is meaningful against plausible harm and deal value. A cap tied to fees paid to date is inadequate even though a cap exists.

mutualCap.title: Mutualcap
mutualCap.description: Whether the cap applies to both sides equally.

consequentialDamagesExcluded.title: Consequentialdamagesexcluded
consequentialDamagesExcluded.description: Whether consequential and indirect damages are excluded.

uncappedCarveouts.title: Uncappedcarveouts
uncappedCarveouts.description: Categories of liability that sit OUTSIDE the cap, for example indemnity or confidentiality breaches.

supercap.title: Supercap
supercap.description: A raised cap that applies to specific categories, when the contract sets one.

indemnityExposure.title: Indemnityexposure
indemnityExposure.description: What you are indemnifying the counterparty for.

insuranceRequired.title: Insurancerequired
insuranceRequired.description: Insurance the contract requires you to carry.

claimTimeBar.title: Claimtimebar
claimTimeBar.description: Any deadline for bringing a claim under the contract.

ReviewLiabilityExposure.title: ReviewLiabilityExposure
ReviewLiabilityExposure.description:
How much the reviewer is on the hook for, in one panel.

Every field is nullable and stays nullable. This is assembled defensively
from LLM output about contract language that may not exist: a contract with
no liability clause has no cap, and `null` is the true answer rather than a
zero that reads as "capped at nothing".

tier.title: Tier
tier.description: Priority tier: 1 is must-have and covers deal breakers, 2 is should-have, 3 is nice-to-have.

items.title: Items
items.description: What to raise at this tier, in order.

ReviewNegotiationPriority.title: ReviewNegotiationPriority
ReviewNegotiationPriority.description: One tier of the negotiation plan: what to raise first, and what to trade.

clauseName.title: Clausename
clauseName.description: Which clause this edit applies to.

sectionReference.title: Sectionreference
sectionReference.description: Where the clause sits in the contract, for example `8.2`.

currentLanguage.title: Currentlanguage
currentLanguage.description: The text to be replaced, as it stands in the contract. Empty for an insertion.

proposedLanguage.title: Proposedlanguage
proposedLanguage.description: The replacement text to send to the counterparty.

rationale.title: Rationale
rationale.description: Why this edit is being proposed. Suitable to put in a margin comment.

priority.title: Priority
priority.description: How hard to push for this edit: `must_have`, `should_have` or `nice_to_have`.

fallbackPosition.title: Fallbackposition
fallbackPosition.description: What to retreat to if this edit is rejected, taken from the playbook's fallback ladder.

grounding.title: Grounding
grounding.description: Whether `currentLanguage` was found verbatim in the contract. `verified` means it was. `unverified` means it was NOT, so the edit may be misanchored. `insertion` means there is nothing to anchor because the clause is missing. An integration applying redlines automatically must stop and ask a human on `unverified`.

approvalLevel.title: Approvallevel
approvalLevel.description: Sign-off this edit needs before it goes out: `none`, `manager`, `partner` or `gc`.

isDealBreaker.title: Isdealbreaker
isDealBreaker.description: True when the clause this edit addresses is at or below the walk-away floor.

nature.title: Nature
nature.description: `substantive` or `housekeeping`. Absent means unclassified, on a review produced before the pipeline classified this. Absent is NOT the same as `housekeeping`.

ReviewRedline.title: ReviewRedline
ReviewRedline.description: One proposed edit, ready to send to counterparty counsel.
